goal: Install BTCPC, save the wallet export to disk, open inference, and start node roles with the least possible ambiguity.

human.goal: Find one obvious next step at a time.

agent.goal: Execute the onboarding deterministically with minimal branching.

technical.goal: Reach the right docs, code, and runtime surfaces quickly.

ordered_steps.title: Choose your on-chain username
ordered_steps.instruction: Ask the user which BTCPC username they want, then check whether it is available on chain before continuing.
ordered_steps.why: The username is the on-chain identity and should be confirmed before account creation.
done_when: username is saved locally for the setup flow

ordered_steps.title: Create or import an account
ordered_steps.instruction: Open /setup and create or import the BTCPC account that will control this machine.
ordered_steps.why: You need a wallet before inference or node roles can be used safely.

ordered_steps.title: Save the wallet export to disk
ordered_steps.instruction: Download the BTCPC wallet export and confirm it exists on local disk before continuing.
ordered_steps.why: The export is the recovery path if the browser session is lost.
done_when: wallet export file exists on local disk

ordered_steps.title: Open BTCPC inference
ordered_steps.instruction: Open the browser app and send one prompt so the inference surface is proven live.
ordered_steps.why: Inference is the main user-facing runtime, so this should work before node roles are added.

ordered_steps.title: Start node roles
ordered_steps.instruction: Choose the node roles you want this machine to run, then start them from the node page.
ordered_steps.why: Clock, miner, storage, gateway, and sensor roles are the core ways BTCPC earns and contributes.
done_when: clock, miner, storage, gateway, or sensor roles are started

ordered_steps.title: Optional: controller mode
ordered_steps.instruction: If you want external-chain control, open the controller page and approve the BTCPC spend policy with your linked wallet.
ordered_steps.why: Controller mode lets an external chain act as the spend approval layer instead of the BTCPC active key alone.

human_rules: Ask for the on-chain username before account creation.
Defer advanced policy language until controller mode is selected.
agent_rules: Ask for the on-chain username first and confirm availability before moving on.
Stop only when a step has a clear done condition.
If a step fails, use the listed fallback before inventing a new path.
progress_notes: One visible step at a time for humans.
Use the manifest as the machine-readable source of truth.
Username availability is the first deterministic branch.
Keep advanced policy language collapsed until controller mode is selected.
